sections.markdown:
## C2 — Confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: points in a year versus convictions in five years, major versus minor violation counts, five-year revocation versus two-year wait, daily versus weekly occupational caps, child seat versus booster ages, lap versus shoulder belt, and own versus borrowed car insurance
Confusable pairs among privilege, safety belt and insurance rules, where several similar numbers measure different things; each block ties to one handbook page, and hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec12-R01 | anchor: A01
The 12-point rule counts demerit points within any 12-month period, while the habitual offender rule counts convictions over five years. [A01]
Why it matters: group privilege loss; confusable points versus convictions.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec12-R02 | anchor: A01
Habitual offender status takes only four major violations but 12 minor ones within five years. [A01]
Why it matters: group habitual offender; confusable major versus minor count.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec12-R03 | anchor: A01
For a habitual traffic offender the revocation lasts five years, but an occupational license may become possible after a two-year wait. [A01]
Why it matters: group habitual offender; confusable revocation length versus waiting period.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec12-R04 | anchor: A01
Point doubling applies to probationary license holders, ID card holders and unlicensed drivers, and starts with the second conviction rather than the first. [A01]
Why it matters: group points; misconception doubling starts on the first conviction.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec12-R05 | anchor: A01
The occupational license caps are 12 hours in a day and 60 hours in a week, and both apply at once. [A01]
Why it matters: group occupational license; confusable daily versus weekly cap.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec12-R06 | anchor: A01
Both getting an occupational license and reinstating a revoked one can require proof of financial responsibility, but only reinstatement adds a fee and proof of identity in the handbook. [A01]
Why it matters: group reinstatement; confusable occupational license versus reinstatement.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec12-R07 | anchor: A02
Medical conditions are reported on the driver license application MV3001, while an invisible disability is disclosed on the separate form MV2167. [A02]
Why it matters: group reporting; confusable medical report versus invisible disability form.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec12-R08 | anchor: A02
The seat belt law covers passengers of any age, not just children or the driver. [A02]
Why it matters: group seat belts; misconception adults in back may ride unbelted.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec12-R09 | anchor: A03
The lap belt goes low across the hip bones, while the shoulder belt crosses the chest with about a fist of room. [A03]
Why it matters: group belt fit; confusable lap versus shoulder belt.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec12-R10 | anchor: A03
A child generally needs a child safety seat until age four and then a booster seat until age eight. [A03]
Why it matters: group child seats; confusable car seat age versus booster age.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec12-R11 | anchor: A03
Out-of-state drivers may show proof of insurance from their home state's company, but anyone driving another person's car must still make sure it is insured. [A03]
Why it matters: group insurance; confusable out-of-state proof versus borrowed car duty.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec12-R12 | anchor: A03
An adult donor's decision, from age 18, cannot be overridden by family, yet the handbook still advises telling your family. [A03]
Why it matters: group organ donation; misconception family can cancel an adult's decision.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0059]
